---
title: "Getting started"
---

## Install

ggp-client needs Python 3.10 or later.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/jossl95/ggp_client
cd ggp_client
pip install -e .
```

## Log in

Downloading needs the access link the portal emails you (request it on the portal's login page). The first
download asks you to paste it; the input is hidden. The session is then saved in `data/.session.json` (readable
only by you) and reused, so the link is needed once. ggp-client looks for a login in this order:

1. the saved session, if it still works;
2. the `access_url` argument (`--access-url` on the command line);
3. the `GGP_ACCESS_URL` environment variable;
4. otherwise it asks. With no terminal to ask on (a scheduled job) it stops with a `LoginError`.

::: {.callout-warning}
The access link works like a password. Do not commit it, and prefer the prompt or the environment variable over
`--access-url`, which stays in your shell history. ggp-client never writes it to its log.
:::

## Index the portal

```bash
ggp-client sync                                     # all datasets into data/catalogue.sqlite
ggp-client list                                     # everything
ggp-client list --project ggs --round 2 --country nl at
ggp-client list --ids 10-25                         # by catalogue id
```

`sync` reads the public dataset pages, then logs in to add the Harmonized Histories and Additional Datasets,
which the portal lists only on the logged-in data access page. Without a login it indexes the rest and says
what it skipped.

## Filters

`list`, `download`, `preprocess` and `consolidate` take the same filters. Each takes one value, several, or
nothing (all). Case does not matter, and a value that is not in the catalogue is an error, not an empty result.

| filter | values |
|---|---|
| `--project` | `ggs`, `ffs`, `hh` (Harmonized Histories), `other` (Additional Datasets), `teaching` |
| `--round` | `1`, `2` (or `i`, `ii`) |
| `--wave` | `w1`, `w2`, `w3`, `pilot`, ...; for `hh` and `other` the dataset name, e.g. `nkps` |
| `--country` | two-letter codes: `nl`, `at`, ... |
| `--ids` | catalogue ids and ranges: `3-12,20` |
| `--all-versions` | also superseded versions (default: the latest only) |

Run `list` first: it shows what the other commands will work on.

## Download

```bash
ggp-client download                              # everything, latest versions, data files only
ggp-client download --project ggs --round 2 --wave w1 --country nl
ggp-client download --ext dta                    # only Stata files (dta, sav, csv: one or several)
ggp-client download --metadata                   # also codebooks, readmes and other documents
ggp-client download --force                      # download again and overwrite
```

Archives (zip, and 7z for most GGS-I wave 1 files and the Harmonized Histories) are unpacked into one folder per
file, keeping their structure; an archive inside the archive becomes a folder. Existing files are never
overwritten, so your own changes survive; asking for more later (another `--ext`, or `--metadata`) adds the
missing files. A download with no matching file is reported as failed and leaves nothing behind.

## Then

```bash
ggp-client preprocess  --project ggs --round 2   # each data file to parquet + meta.json
ggp-client consolidate --project ggs --round 2   # one dataset per round and wave
```

See the [GGS-II use case](ggs-ii.qmd) for what these produce. Every step is logged, with time stamps, to
`data/ggp_client.log`.
